title: Dedicated throughput blackbox runner and customer sign-off kit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reproducible, blackbox-oriented throughput runner and an associated customer sign-off kit that 1) runs steady-state and burst workloads against Dedicated pools, 2) exercises autoscaling policies and fleet controls, and 3) produces a standardized report and checklist customers can use to accept capacity commits. This ticket covers runner code, canonical workload taxonomy, automated analysis scripts, and a runbook for operator + customer handoff.
acceptance_criteria: A runnable CLI and CI job that executes canonical workloads (steady-state, burst, tail-stress, tenant-mix) against a target Dedicated pool
Generated report includes throughput (tokens/s), p50/p95/p99 latency, per-GPU utilization, batching stats, and autoscaler events with timestamps
Runner can replay a real customer traffic trace (sanitized) and a synthetic steady-state profile with parameterized qps and prompt length
Automated analysis flags regressions: >10% throughput drop or >2x p99 increase relative to baseline; thresholds configurable per-run
Customer sign-off kit (PDF + checklist) with run templates, expected tolerance ranges, and interpretation guidance
Run completes end-to-end in CI (smoke) and has a documented manual procedure for customer on-site runs
steps: Design workload taxonomy: define steady-state, 95/5 burst mix, cold-start spike, KV-heavy prompts, and long-context scenarios
Implement blackbox runner (go template): HTTP/gRPC request generator, rate controller, prompt bank loader, and KV cache toggles
Instrument telemetry capture: token counters, batching histograms, GPU metrics (util, mem), autoscaler logs, and request traces
Add replay adapter to feed sanitized customer traces and map to runner's rate controller
Create analysis scripts: ingest telemetry, compute baselines, produce PDF/CSV report and change summary
Write customer sign-off kit: checklist, pass/fail criteria, required artifacts (raw traces, reports), and run templates
Integrate smoke job into CI and publish a Confluence runbook and Datadog dashboard link
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Blackbox vs whitebox: we intentionally keep runner blackbox (no runtime hooks) to mirror customer-facing experience; whitebox probes will live in a separate internal harness

Synthetic vs replay: default baseline uses synthetic steady-state to ensure reproducibility; replay mode is available for higher-fidelity acceptance testing but requires sanitized traces and longer run time
Autoscaler exercise: we run both conservative and aggressive autoscaler policies; conservative policy is default for customer sign-off to avoid noisy failures during demo
Latency vs throughput: report highlights both but we favor throughput stability (sustain) in sign-off criteria while flagging tail latency regressions for follow-up
